title: What's New — Real-World Video + CPU Sensor Proof
summary: PulseGuard v0.6.4 replaces the synthetic-only playback proof with a real-world user-supplied video derivative looped for the full 3-minute stability window, separates visible playback from modern Windows MediaPlayer / Media Foundation decoder evidence, and adds an explicit-consent PawnIO 2.2.0 bootstrap so LibreHardwareMonitor can reach supported CPU package/core sensors without ever converting missing CPU evidence into a false PASS.

items.heading: Real-world video for the full three minutes
items.detail: PulseGuard packages a 1280x720 60 FPS H.264/AAC derivative of user-owned real-world footage and loops it throughout the 180-second stability test. Lower-end PCs are not failed merely for failing to sustain the source video's original 1440p120 capture rate.

items.heading: Decoder proof is independent from the window
items.detail: The H.264 workload uses the modern Windows MediaPlayer frame-server path backed by the Windows media stack / Media Foundation. PASS requires decoded frame events, decoder/media progress, and non-zero decoded dimensions. WPF presentation FPS or visible motion alone can never promote a failed decoder to PASS.

items.heading: Actual footage is visible
items.detail: The visible WPF presentation uses a compatibility derivative of the same real-world footage. The PulseGuard visible motion fallback remains available if WPF presentation fails, but fallback motion is presentation evidence only and is never counted as decoder proof.

items.heading: Verified PawnIO 2.2.0 CPU sensor bootstrap
items.detail: When PawnIO is absent, PulseGuard asks for explicit one-time consent before installing the kernel sensor driver. It downloads only the pinned official PawnIO 2.2.0 installer, verifies SHA-256, requires a Valid Authenticode signature from the expected publisher identity, re-verifies immediately before execution, and accepts only success or reboot-required installer exit codes.

items.heading: CPU temperature still cannot fake PASS
items.detail: After PawnIO setup, the stability worker starts in a fresh process and retries LibreHardwareMonitor CPU telemetry. If a real CPU temperature sensor is still unavailable—or a reboot is required—Temperature remains WARNING and GPU/SSD/ACPI temperatures cannot substitute for CPU evidence.

items.heading: Visible PREPARING / RUNNING state retained
items.detail: The 3-minute worker continues to publish PREPARING before evidence setup and RUNNING as active CPU/RAM/disk/graphics load begins, so sensor-provider setup cannot make the whole panel look frozen.

items.heading: Cleaner stereo chime retained
items.detail: Sound continues to use the cleaner PulseGuard stereo chime that identifies left channel, right channel, then both channels, without replaying an annoying alert every 30 seconds.

items.heading: Evidence & Accuracy contracts retained
items.detail: Repair verification still uses VERIFIED_FIXED, IMPROVED, NOT_FIXED, REBOOT_REQUIRED, UNVERIFIED and NO_CHANGE_NEEDED; WHEA evidence remains scoped to the exact test window; driver provenance remains recorded; unsupported VRAM integrity remains N/A; and PulseGuard does not claim per-driver latency attribution without equivalent evidence.

items.heading: Clean Runtime layout retained
items.detail: PulseGuard PC.vbs remains the obvious customer launcher. Internal engines, rules, assets, driver catalog and notices remain under Runtime while compatibility bridge files preserve updates and existing shortcuts.
